question: How does Cloud SQL help organizations create business insights?

options.A: Integrates with business intelligence and analytics platforms
options.B: Generates predictions using machine learning models
options.C: Generates real-time charts and intelligent analytics
options.D: Transforms business data from unstructured to structured

explanations.A: Correct. Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server) that integrates with business intelligence and analytics tools such as Looker, so organizations can query and visualize the stored data to derive insights.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Generating predictions with machine learning is the job of services like Vertex AI or BigQuery ML, not Cloud SQL, which is an operational relational database.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Producing real-time charts and intelligent analytics is the role of visualization/BI tools like Looker, not the database engine itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud SQL stores structured relational data; it does not transform unstructured data into structured data.

question: An organization recently launched a virtual customer support agent, generating vast amounts of text and speech data. Why should they use a cloud data warehouse to interpret this data?

options.A: To natively visualize both types of data using a dashboard in real time
options.B: To ingest and analyze structured and unstructured data at scale, in real time
options.C: To secure data transmission between cloud and on-premises environments
options.D: To transform data from structured to unstructured

explanations.A: Incorrect. A data warehouse is for storage and analytics; visualization is handled by separate BI/dashboard tools, so native real-time visualization is not the primary reason.
explanations.B: Correct. A cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery can ingest and analyze large volumes of both structured and unstructured (or semi-structured) data at scale and in near real time, which is ideal for interpreting text and speech data.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Securing data transmission between environments is a networking/security concern (e.g., VPN, encryption), not the purpose of a data warehouse.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A data warehouse is used to analyze data, not to convert structured data into unstructured data.

question: An organization wants to add a new function to their application. They want to write the code and let the public cloud provider handle the infrastructure. Which infrastructure solution should they use?

options.A: Virtual machines
options.B: Bare Metal Solution
options.C: Serverless computing
options.D: Container Registry

explanations.A: Incorrect. With virtual machines (Compute Engine) the customer is still responsible for managing the operating system and scaling the infrastructure.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Bare Metal Solution provides dedicated physical hardware, placing even more infrastructure management on the customer, the opposite of what is wanted.
explanations.C: Correct. Serverless computing (e.g., Cloud Functions or Cloud Run) lets developers write and deploy code while Google fully manages the underlying infrastructure, provisioning, and scaling.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Container Registry (now Artifact Registry) is a repository for storing container images, not a compute solution for running code.

question: An organization wants to leverage tooling and automation as part of its new DevOps philosophy. Which operational challenge will this resolve?

options.A: Repetitive manual tasks that hinder workflows
options.B: Time-consuming supervision of creative tasks
options.C: Distribution and supply-chain issues
options.D: Defective technical equipment that limits innovation

explanations.A: Correct. A core goal of DevOps is to reduce toil by automating repetitive manual tasks, which speeds workflows and frees teams to focus on higher-value work.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Automation targets repetitive, predictable toil, not the supervision of creative work, which inherently requires human judgment.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Distribution and supply-chain logistics are business operations unrelated to DevOps software-delivery automation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. DevOps tooling automates software processes; it does not repair defective physical equipment.

question: An organization needs to store structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data in its raw, native format in the same repository. Which cloud data management solution should the organization use?

options.A: Data field
options.B: Data lake
options.C: Database
options.D: Data warehouse

explanations.A: Incorrect. A 'data field' is a single attribute within a record, not a repository for storing diverse data types.
explanations.B: Correct. A data lake stores structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data in its raw, native format within a single repository, making it the right choice.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A database (especially relational) is designed for structured data with a predefined schema, not raw mixed-format data.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A data warehouse stores processed, structured data optimized for analytics, not raw unstructured data in native format.

question: An organization wants its users to validate a series of new features for their app. Why should they use App Engine?

options.A: Because their app is containerized and enabled by microservices
options.B: Because the updated app will only include new features
options.C: To run different versions of the app for different users
options.D: To run different versions of the app for the same user

explanations.A: Incorrect. While App Engine can run code, being containerized is not the reason it helps validate new features through user testing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The updated app including only new features is not a capability that App Engine provides for feature validation.
explanations.C: Correct. App Engine supports traffic splitting across multiple deployed versions, so different users can be routed to different versions, enabling A/B testing and validation of new features.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Validation works by exposing different versions to different user groups; serving multiple versions to the same single user is not how feature testing is performed.

question: How would an organization benefit from using Looker?

options.A: Optimal identity and access management
options.B: Leading serverless warehousing technology
options.C: Robust data roll-back accuracy
options.D: Advanced business intelligence and analytics

explanations.A: Incorrect. Identity and access management is provided by Cloud IAM and Cloud Identity, not Looker.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Serverless data warehousing is provided by BigQuery; Looker connects to such warehouses but is not itself the warehouse.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Data roll-back and recovery are database/backup capabilities, not what Looker delivers.
explanations.D: Correct. Looker is Google Cloud's business intelligence platform, providing advanced data exploration, modeling, dashboards, and analytics.

question: An organization delivers a proactive healthcare service. They want to efficiently and automatically collect patient data. What should the organization encourage the patients to do?

options.A: Use at-home health screening devices and then upload their health data daily
options.B: Wear Internet of Things (IoT) devices that upload their health data in real time
options.C: Self-assess their health data and then document and upload it in real time
options.D: Visit a nurse who will use Internet of Things (IoT) devices to collect and upload their health data

explanations.A: Incorrect. Manually uploading data daily is neither continuous nor fully automatic, so it does not meet the requirement for efficient automatic collection.
explanations.B: Correct. Wearable IoT devices automatically and continuously stream patient data in real time, enabling efficient, hands-off data collection that supports proactive healthcare.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Self-assessment and manual documentation require human effort and are not automatic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Requiring patients to visit a nurse is neither efficient nor automatic, and it introduces manual, location-dependent steps.

question: How would a global organization benefit from managing their data with Cloud Spanner?

options.A: Cloud Spanner is optimized for cold storage
options.B: Cloud Spanner replicates data across regions in real time
options.C: Cloud Spanner is optimized to ingest unstructured data
options.D: Cloud Spanner visualizes and analyzes data in real time

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cold storage is a low-cost archival tier of Cloud Storage; Cloud Spanner is a high-performance transactional database, not cold storage.
explanations.B: Correct. Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed, strongly consistent relational database that synchronously replicates data across regions, giving a global organization low-latency, highly available access worldwide.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Spanner is a relational (structured) database; ingesting unstructured data is not its purpose.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Visualization and analytics are handled by tools like Looker and BigQuery, not by the Spanner transactional database.

question: An employee receives an email from their internet service provider asking for their bank account number and password. Which cybersecurity threat is this?

options.A: Ransomware
options.B: Distributed Denial of Service
options.C: Spamming
options.D: Phishing

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ransomware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment for their release; it does not solicit credentials via email.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A Distributed Denial of Service overwhelms a service with traffic to make it unavailable; it does not request personal information.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Spamming is unsolicited bulk messaging; while annoying, it is not specifically the deceptive solicitation of sensitive credentials.
explanations.D: Correct. Phishing is a social-engineering attack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted entity (here, the ISP) to trick the victim into revealing sensitive information like bank details and passwords.

question: An organization wants to move from a tactical cloud adoption approach to a transformational approach. How should they adapt the way they lead the organization?

options.A: Increase top-down visibility and foster a culture of blamelessness
options.B: Shift from an operational expenditure model to capital expenditure
options.C: Drive cloud adoption with an individual contributor focus
options.D: Invest in on-premises infrastructure to redesign relationships between IT and employees

explanations.A: Correct. A transformational approach requires leadership change: increasing top-down visibility and fostering a blameless culture encourages experimentation, learning, and organization-wide change.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud adoption typically shifts spending toward operational expenditure, not toward capital expenditure, and this is a financial detail, not a leadership transformation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Transformation is driven by leadership and culture across the organization, not by focusing on individual contributors in isolation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Investing further in on-premises infrastructure runs counter to a transformational cloud-adoption strategy.

question: Why is data stored in Google Cloud secure and private?

options.A: Data is encrypted by the Security Command Center
options.B: Data is encrypted by Cloud Data Loss Prevention
options.C: Data is encrypted by default
options.D: Data is encrypted when an appropriate tag is applied

explanations.A: Incorrect. Security Command Center is a security and risk management/monitoring platform; it does not perform data encryption.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Data Loss Prevention discovers, classifies, and de-identifies sensitive data, but it is not what encrypts stored data.
explanations.C: Correct. Google Cloud encrypts customer data at rest by default, with no action required by the customer, which is a core reason the data is secure and private.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Encryption at rest is automatic and does not depend on applying a tag.

question: An organization wants to use multiple marketing datasets to forecast user acquisition. How should they use cloud technology to gain new insights from the data?

options.A: Import the datasets into a custom data warehouse, and then archive old data
options.B: Import and selectively archive the datasets in a custom data lake
options.C: Separate the datasets and make predictions using machine learning
options.D: Combine the datasets and make predictions using machine learning

explanations.A: Incorrect. Simply importing and archiving data does not produce forecasts or new predictive insights.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Archiving data in a data lake stores it but does not generate the predictions needed to forecast user acquisition.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Keeping the datasets separate limits the richness of the analysis; combining them gives the model more signal for accurate forecasting.
explanations.D: Correct. Combining the multiple marketing datasets and applying machine learning lets the organization find patterns across all the data and generate predictions to forecast user acquisition.

question: An organization wants to collect metrics and metadata from their cloud applications and put them into dashboards. Which Google Cloud tool should they use?

options.A: Cloud Monitoring
options.B: Cloud Trace
options.C: Cloud Logging
options.D: Cloud Debugger

explanations.A: Correct. Cloud Monitoring collects metrics and metadata from applications and infrastructure and presents them in dashboards, charts, and alerts.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Trace analyzes application latency and request paths in distributed systems, not general metrics dashboards.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Logging stores and queries log entries; collecting metrics into dashboards is the role of Cloud Monitoring.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud Debugger inspects running application code; it does not build metrics dashboards.

question: A manager wants to review Google Cloud data access among their employees. Who is responsible for defining data access policies?

options.A: Cloud Identity
options.B: Google Cloud Customer Care team
options.C: Their organization's IT team
options.D: Their organization's end users

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Identity is a tool used to manage users and groups; it is a service, not the party that decides what the access policies should be.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Under the shared responsibility model, Google's Customer Care team supports the platform but does not define a customer's internal data access policies.
explanations.C: Correct. In the shared responsibility model, the customer (the organization's IT team) is responsible for managing identities and defining who may access their data and resources.
explanations.D: Incorrect. End users consume resources according to assigned permissions; they do not set the organization's access policies.

question: An organization has decided to modernize their applications in the cloud to keep up with their customers' needs. What may have prompted this business decision?

options.A: Their on-premises applications only autoscale to meet demand.
options.B: They want to change from a pay-as-you-go model to a capital expenditure model.
options.C: Their source code changes erroneously without developer interaction.
options.D: Their on-premises applications take months to update and deploy.

explanations.A: Incorrect. On-premises applications generally do not autoscale easily; autoscaling is a cloud benefit, so this is not a problem prompting modernization.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud modernization shifts spending toward operational expenditure (pay-as-you-go), not toward capital expenditure.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Source code does not change on its own without developer action; this is not a realistic driver.
explanations.D: Correct. Slow, months-long update and deployment cycles for on-premises applications are a common pain point that prompts organizations to modernize in the cloud for faster, more agile releases.

question: An organization needs to categorize a large group of photographs using pre-trained machine learning. Which Google Cloud product or service should the organization use?

options.A: Vision API
options.B: BigQuery ML
options.C: AutoML Vision
options.D: Looker

explanations.A: Correct. The Vision API is a pre-trained machine learning service that classifies images, detects objects, and labels content without requiring the customer to train a model.
explanations.B: Incorrect. BigQuery ML lets users build and train custom models using SQL on data in BigQuery; it is not a pre-trained image categorization service.
explanations.C: Incorrect. AutoML Vision is for training a custom image model on your own labeled data, which is not 'pre-trained.'
explanations.D: Incorrect. Looker is a business intelligence and analytics platform and cannot categorize photographs with machine learning.

question: An organization provides a loyalty program for its customers. It recently partnered with other businesses so that customers can get loyalty points at a range of other stores. Why should the organization use application programming interfaces (APIs)?

options.A: To migrate all partner data for disaster recovery
options.B: To analyze and publish loyalty program statistics to a dashboard
options.C: To personalize recommendations for loyalty card users
options.D: To connect third-party systems to ensure up-to-date information

explanations.A: Incorrect. Migrating data for disaster recovery is a backup/resilience activity, not the purpose of APIs for partner integration.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Analyzing and publishing statistics is a BI/dashboard function, not why APIs are needed to connect partners.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Personalizing recommendations is a machine learning/analytics task, not the core role of APIs here.
explanations.D: Correct. APIs let the organization connect its systems with third-party partner systems so loyalty point information stays synchronized and up to date across all stores in real time.

question: A travel agency wants to seamlessly share their social media content with partners. What should the organization use?

options.A: A NoSQL database
options.B: Anthos Config Management
options.C: The App Engine standard environment
options.D: An application programming interface (API)

explanations.A: Incorrect. A NoSQL database stores data; it does not provide a standardized way to share content with external partners.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Anthos Config Management enforces configuration policy across Kubernetes clusters; it is unrelated to sharing social media content.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The App Engine standard environment is a platform for hosting applications, not a mechanism for content sharing between organizations.
explanations.D: Correct. An API provides a standardized, secure interface that lets the travel agency seamlessly share its social media content and data with partner systems.

question: How do out-of-the-box APIs make artificial intelligence and machine learning more accessible for all Google Cloud customers?

options.A: They don't require technical specialists.
options.B: They don't require data input and validation.
options.C: They require fewer security permissions.
options.D: They all require custom training models.

explanations.A: Correct. Pre-trained, out-of-the-box ML APIs (like the Vision or Speech-to-Text APIs) can be called directly without data science expertise, making AI/ML accessible to customers who lack specialist staff.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Customers still must supply and validate input data; the APIs do not eliminate the need for data input.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Out-of-the-box APIs do not inherently reduce the security permissions required; standard IAM and authentication still apply.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The whole point of out-of-the-box APIs is that they are pre-trained and do not require custom training models.

question: An organization needs to migrate specialized workloads to the cloud while maintaining their existing complex licensing and architecture. What Google Cloud solution should the organization use?

options.A: Compute Engine
options.B: Bare Metal Solution
options.C: Cloud Run
options.D: Cloud Functions

explanations.A: Incorrect. Compute Engine provides virtual machines, but certain specialized workloads with complex licensing (for example, some Oracle deployments) require dedicated physical hardware, not VMs.
explanations.B: Correct. Bare Metal Solution provides dedicated, single-tenant physical servers near Google Cloud, letting organizations lift specialized workloads with their existing licensing and architecture intact.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Run is a serverless container platform and cannot preserve complex legacy licensing or specialized hardware architecture.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud Functions is an event-driven serverless service for small functions, unsuited to migrating specialized, license-bound workloads.

question: An organization finds that the amount of cash in their vending machines doesn't match the value of items sold. They have decided to upgrade their vending machines with cloud-based mobile payment systems. How could the organization benefit from this upgrade?

options.A: They could relax data access permissions.
options.B: They could reduce their error budget overspend.
options.C: They could improve their perimeter security.
options.D: They could view data history to see transactions.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Relaxing data access permissions weakens security and does nothing to reconcile cash discrepancies.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An error budget is an SRE concept about acceptable service unreliability and is unrelated to reconciling vending machine payments.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Perimeter (network) security does not address the financial reconciliation problem described.
explanations.D: Correct. Cloud-based mobile payments create a digital record of every transaction, so the organization can view transaction history to track sales and reconcile discrepancies.

question: A food delivery service needs access to real-time menu information from all partner restaurants. They also need to share customer order information with the restaurants in real time. What should the organization use?

options.A: Site reliability engineering (SRE)
options.B: An application programming interface (API)
options.C: A customized machine learning model
options.D: A multi-regional database

explanations.A: Incorrect. SRE is a discipline for operating reliable services; it is not a mechanism for exchanging real-time data between partner systems.
explanations.B: Correct. An API provides a standardized interface to exchange real-time menu and order information bidirectionally between the food delivery service and partner restaurants.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A custom machine learning model makes predictions; it does not connect systems to exchange live menu and order data.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A multi-regional database stores data with geographic redundancy but does not by itself integrate the delivery service with external partner systems.

question: An organization is planning to create many new applications and needs a system for managing and orchestrating their containers. Why should they use Google Kubernetes Engine?

options.A: It enables rapid application deployment and testing.
options.B: It optimizes virtual machine performance.
options.C: It connects legacy systems to an application.
options.D: It provides pre-written source code for application development.

explanations.A: Correct. Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) is a managed container orchestration platform that automates deployment, scaling, and management of containers, enabling rapid and consistent application deployment and testing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. GKE orchestrates containers; tuning individual virtual machine performance is not its purpose.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Connecting legacy systems is typically done with APIs or integration tools, not the role of a container orchestrator.
explanations.D: Incorrect. GKE does not supply pre-written application source code; it runs and manages the containers you provide.

question: How does Google Cloud enable customers to leverage the power of artificial intelligence and machine learning?

options.A: With scalable on-premises tensor processing units
options.B: With APIs and tools for users at different levels of expertise
options.C: With affordable and scalable quantum computing
options.D: With machine learning models that always require custom training

explanations.A: Incorrect. Tensor Processing Units are offered as scalable cloud resources, not as on-premises hardware.
explanations.B: Correct. Google Cloud offers a spectrum of AI/ML options, from pre-trained APIs for non-experts to customizable tools like Vertex AI and BigQuery ML for advanced users, meeting customers at different expertise levels.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Quantum computing is experimental and is not the way Google Cloud broadly delivers AI/ML to customers.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Many Google Cloud ML offerings are pre-trained and do not require custom training, so 'always require custom training' is false.

question: An online retail organization wants to optimize their service. What is an example of unstructured data that they can use to make decisions?

options.A: Customer survey comments
options.B: Seller location coordinates
options.C: Product sales trends
options.D: Warehouse inventory records

explanations.A: Correct. Free-form customer survey comments are unstructured text data because they do not fit neatly into a predefined schema of rows and columns.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Location coordinates are structured numeric values that fit clearly defined fields.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Product sales trends are derived from structured, quantitative records organized in tables.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Warehouse inventory records are structured data stored in defined fields such as SKU, quantity, and location.

question: An organization's public cloud provider failed to meet their SLA of 99.99% availability. What is the potential impact on the organization?

options.A: The organization risks using up their error budget.
options.B: Renegotiation of the SLA to put less emphasis on uptime could be necessary.
options.C: Unexpected downtime could risk the loss of customers.
options.D: All data stored in their database could be unexpectedly lost.

explanations.A: Incorrect. An error budget is an internal SRE measure the organization sets for its own services; missing a provider's SLA does not directly consume the organization's error budget in this scenario.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Renegotiating the SLA to de-emphasize uptime is not an impact of the breach and would not address the harm caused by downtime.
explanations.C: Correct. When the provider misses the availability SLA, the resulting unexpected downtime can disrupt the organization's services, frustrate users, and risk the loss of customers.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An availability SLA breach concerns uptime, not data durability; it does not imply all stored data is lost.

question: An organization needs to train a machine learning model to categorize photographs. Which Google Cloud product or service should the organization use?

options.A: Video Intelligence API
options.B: AutoML Vision
options.C: BigQuery ML
options.D: Looker

explanations.A: Incorrect. The Video Intelligence API analyzes video content and is pre-trained, not a tool for training a custom image classification model.
explanations.B: Correct. AutoML Vision lets organizations train a custom image classification model on their own labeled photographs without deep ML expertise, which matches the need to train a model to categorize photos.
explanations.C: Incorrect. BigQuery ML builds models from structured/tabular data using SQL and is not designed for training image classifiers from photographs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Looker is a business intelligence platform and cannot train machine learning models for image categorization.

question: A multinational organization has decided to use public cloud services to modernize their IT infrastructure. What is one benefit of doing this?

options.A: They can perform hardware maintenance outside of normal business hours.
options.B: They can expect 100% service availability in all regions.
options.C: Built-in security is no longer required during data migrations.
options.D: Access to data and computer resources is not tied to a geographical location.

explanations.A: Incorrect. With public cloud, the provider manages the physical hardware, so customers no longer perform hardware maintenance at all.
explanations.B: Incorrect. No provider guarantees 100% availability; SLAs offer high but not perfect uptime.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Security remains essential during migrations under the shared responsibility model; it is never eliminated.
explanations.D: Correct. The public cloud lets a multinational organization access data and compute resources globally over the internet, removing dependence on a single physical location.

question: An organization meets their service level objective (SLO) of 99.999% (`five nines`). How much downtime do their end users experience per year?

options.A: 5 minutes
options.B: 500 minutes
options.C: 5 hours
options.D: 5 days

explanations.A: Correct. 'Five nines' (99.999%) availability allows only about 5.26 minutes of downtime per year, which rounds to roughly 5 minutes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. About 500 minutes per year corresponds to roughly 99.9% availability, not five nines.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 5 hours of downtime is far more than five nines allows and corresponds to lower availability levels.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 5 days of downtime represents very low availability, nowhere near 99.999%.

question: An organization wants to introduce a new image recognition login system. What should the organization do to follow SRE principles?

options.A: Roll out the new system to a subset of employees to test it out.
options.B: Roll out the new system to all employees to collect as much data as possible.
options.C: Avoid rolling out the new system because it may have security flaws.
options.D: Avoid rolling out the new system because it may violate privacy policy.

explanations.A: Correct. Site Reliability Engineering favors gradual, canary-style rollouts to a small subset of users first, limiting risk and allowing issues to be caught before a full release.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Rolling out to everyone at once contradicts SRE's incremental rollout practice and maximizes the blast radius of any failure.
explanations.C: Incorrect. SRE manages and mitigates risk rather than avoiding all change; refusing to deploy outright is not the SRE approach.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Avoiding deployment entirely is not an SRE principle; SRE balances reliability with the need to ship new features safely.

question: What does Cloud Debugger help an organization do?

options.A: Implement code updates in real time without affecting the service level objective (SLO).
options.B: Inspect source code in real time without affecting user downtime.
options.C: Manage code and accelerate application development.
options.D: Analyze live source code during user downtime.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Debugger inspects running code; it does not deploy or implement code updates.
explanations.B: Correct. Cloud Debugger lets developers inspect the state of running application source code in real time, in production, without stopping the application or causing downtime for users.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Managing source code and accelerating development is the role of source repositories and CI/CD tools, not the debugger.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The value of Cloud Debugger is that it works on live applications without requiring downtime, so 'during user downtime' is wrong.

question: How can a streaming service meet global compliance requirements using the cloud?

options.A: By automatically encrypting personally identifiable information
options.B: By obtaining a business license to operate in a new market
options.C: By allowing users to disable two-factor authentication
options.D: By adhering only to data polices of the country in which the head office is registered

explanations.A: Correct. Automatically encrypting personally identifiable information helps the streaming service protect user data and satisfy data-protection and privacy regulations across the different regions it operates in.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A business operating license is a legal/regulatory matter for entering a market, not a cloud capability for meeting data compliance requirements.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Allowing users to disable two-factor authentication weakens security and would undermine, not support, compliance.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Global compliance requires adhering to the data laws of every region in which users reside, not just the head office's country.

question: An organization wants full control of their virtual machine infrastructure for a custom home-grown application with a product that autoscales and automatically updates. Which Google Cloud product or solution should the organization use?

options.A: Cloud Build
options.B: Cloud Run
options.C: Compute Engine
options.D: App Engine

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Build is a CI/CD service for building and testing code; it does not provide virtual machine infrastructure to run an application.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Run is a serverless container platform that abstracts away the VM infrastructure, so it does not give full control of virtual machines.
explanations.C: Correct. Compute Engine provides full control over virtual machines while still offering managed instance groups that autoscale and support automatic updates, fitting a custom application that needs VM-level control.
explanations.D: Incorrect. App Engine is a fully managed platform that hides the underlying VM infrastructure, so it does not offer full control of virtual machines.

question: An organization wants to build an entirely new infrastructure and applications in the cloud. Which application modernization approach should the organization use?

options.A: Move the application to the cloud, and then change it.
options.B: Change their application, and then move it to the cloud.
options.C: Invent in greenfield.
options.D: Invent in brownfield.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Moving an existing application then changing it (lift-and-shift then improve) assumes there is an existing application, not building entirely new infrastructure from scratch.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Changing an existing application before moving it still starts from existing software rather than inventing something brand new.
explanations.C: Correct. A 'greenfield' approach means building entirely new infrastructure and applications from scratch in the cloud, with no legacy constraints, which matches the requirement.
explanations.D: Incorrect. 'Brownfield' refers to working within existing legacy systems and constraints, the opposite of building everything new.

question: An organization wants to upskill their IT staff. How can they do this in a transformational way?

options.A: Prioritize training current employees instead of hiring new recruits with cloud experience.
options.B: Prioritize giving privileged access to third-party partners and contractors to fill IT knowledge gaps.
options.C: Create a culture of self-motivated, isolated learning with official training materials.
options.D: Create a culture of continuous peer-to-peer learning with official training materials.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A transformational organization blends training existing staff with hiring experienced talent rather than excluding new recruits.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Relying on contractors for knowledge does not build the internal capability and culture that transformation requires.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Isolated learning limits knowledge sharing; transformation depends on collaborative, shared learning.
explanations.D: Correct. Fostering a culture of continuous, peer-to-peer learning supported by official training materials spreads knowledge across teams and is the transformational way to upskill staff.

question: Several departments in an organization are working together on a project. The organization wants to customize access to resources for each department. What is the quickest and most efficient way to achieve this?

options.A: By mapping IAM roles to job functions for each department
options.B: By assigning IAM primitive roles to each employee
options.C: By applying ג€least-privilegeג€ to roles for each employee
options.D: By creating a single shared service account for all departments

explanations.A: Correct. Mapping IAM predefined roles to the job functions of each department grants appropriate, granular access efficiently and is the recommended Google Cloud practice for customizing access at scale.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Primitive roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) are broad and coarse-grained, so they cannot finely customize access per department and violate least-privilege.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Applying least privilege individually to every employee is sound in principle but slow and inefficient compared with mapping roles to job functions.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A single shared service account for all departments removes per-department customization and accountability and is a security anti-pattern.

question: An organization notices that some of their cloud expenditures are too high. What should the organization do to control costs?

options.A: Streamline the hardware procurement process to reduce costs.
options.B: Share cost views with the departments to establish more accountability.
options.C: Change the cost model from operational expenditure to capital expenditure.
options.D: Ensure that all could resources are tagged with a single tag.

explanations.A: Incorrect. In the public cloud the provider owns the hardware, so streamlining hardware procurement does not address cloud spending.
explanations.B: Correct. Sharing cost visibility with each department creates accountability so teams can see and manage their own consumption, a key practice for controlling cloud costs.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud spending is operational expenditure (pay-as-you-go); reverting to capital expenditure runs counter to the cloud model and does not control usage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Effective cost tracking uses multiple meaningful labels (by team, project, environment); a single tag for all resources provides no useful breakdown.

question: What is monitoring within the context of cloud operations?

options.A: Observing cloud expenditure in real time to ensure that budgets are not exceeded
options.B: Collecting predefined and custom metrics from applications and infrastructure
options.C: Tracking user activities to guarantee compliance with privacy regulations
options.D: Tracing user location to document regional access and utilization

explanations.A: Incorrect. Observing expenditure against budgets is cost management/billing, not operations monitoring.
explanations.B: Correct. In cloud operations, monitoring means collecting predefined and custom metrics from applications and infrastructure to observe their health and performance, as Cloud Monitoring does.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tracking user activities for compliance is auditing/logging, not the definition of monitoring.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tracing user location for regional access is not what operational monitoring means.

question: An organization wants to create a new application in the cloud to replace an existing on-premises application. Which application modernization approach should the organization use?

options.A: Move the application to the cloud, and then change it.
options.B: Change their application, and then move it to the cloud.
options.C: Invent in greenfield.
options.D: Invent in brownfield.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Moving the existing application then changing it is a lift-and-shift approach that keeps the legacy app, rather than creating a new one to replace it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Changing the existing application before moving it still reuses the legacy software rather than building a replacement.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pure greenfield means building with no relationship to any existing system; here the new app must account for and replace an existing on-premises application, which involves legacy context.
explanations.D: Correct. A 'brownfield' approach builds the new application while taking the existing on-premises application and its constraints into account, which fits creating a cloud replacement for a legacy app.

question: Why should an organization consider the total cost of ownership (TCO) when moving from on-premises to the cloud?

options.A: To evaluate error budget
options.B: To understand service level availability
options.C: To evaluate return on investment
options.D: To calculate required compute power

explanations.A: Incorrect. An error budget is an SRE reliability concept and is not the reason to assess total cost of ownership.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Service level availability concerns uptime commitments, not the financial comparison TCO provides.
explanations.C: Correct. Calculating TCO (all direct and indirect costs) lets the organization compare on-premises versus cloud spending and evaluate the return on investment of the move.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Calculating required compute power is a capacity-planning exercise, not the purpose of a TCO analysis.

question: How does Google Cloud ensure that customer data remains secure and private when at rest?

options.A: By aggregating training data for customers within each industry
options.B: By automatically locking files containing suspicious code
options.C: By auditing platform privacy practices against industry standards
options.D: By providing privacy reviews for critical customer applications

explanations.A: Incorrect. Aggregating customers' data for training would harm privacy; Google does not use customer data this way to keep it secure.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Automatically locking files with suspicious code is a malware-response action, not how data privacy at rest is assured.
explanations.C: Correct. Google Cloud undergoes independent audits of its privacy and security practices against recognized industry standards and certifications, giving customers assurance their data at rest is handled securely and privately.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Privacy reviews of individual customer applications are a customer responsibility under the shared responsibility model, not how Google assures data privacy at rest.

question: An organization's developers are growing increasingly frustrated by the limitations of their on-premises infrastructure. How would they benefit from leveraging cloud technology?

options.A: They can expect 100% service availability.
options.B: They can avoid the limitations of serverless computing.
options.C: They can have new tools to innovate and optimize resource usage.
options.D: They can optimize maintenance for their on-premises infrastructure.

explanations.A: Incorrect. No cloud provider guarantees 100% availability; this is not a realistic benefit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Moving to the cloud gives access to serverless options rather than avoiding them, and serverless is a benefit, not a limitation to escape.
explanations.C: Correct. The cloud gives developers a broad set of managed services and tools to innovate faster and scale resources elastically, optimizing resource usage and removing on-premises constraints.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adopting the cloud reduces the burden of on-premises maintenance rather than optimizing it; the goal is to move away from those limitations.

question: How is service availability measured in the context of cloud technology?

options.A: Number of available regions
options.B: Percentage of uptime
options.C: Speed of response time
options.D: Number of downtime incidents

explanations.A: Incorrect. The number of available regions describes geographic reach, not the availability of a service.
explanations.B: Correct. Service availability is expressed as a percentage of uptime over a period (for example, 99.9% or 99.999%), which is how SLAs and SLOs define it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Response time speed measures latency or performance, which is a separate metric from availability.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Counting downtime incidents alone does not capture availability; availability is the proportion of time the service is up.

question: An organization wants a cost-effective relational database. Which Google Cloud service should the organization use?

options.A: Cloud Storage
options.B: BigQuery
options.C: Cloud SQL
options.D: Dataflow

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud Storage is object storage for unstructured files (blobs), not a relational database.
explanations.B: Incorrect. BigQuery is a serverless data warehouse for large-scale analytics, not a transactional relational database.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud SQL is Google Cloud's fully managed, cost-effective relational database service supporting MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dataflow is a stream and batch data-processing service, not a database for storing relational data.

question: An organization is altering their gaming product so that it is compatible with cloud technology. What can they expect when moving from traditional technology to cloud technology?

options.A: No change to existing responsibilities
options.B: A shift toward OpEx
options.C: A shift toward using structured data
options.D: Increased hardware maintenance

explanations.A: Incorrect. Moving to the cloud changes responsibilities under the shared responsibility model, so 'no change' is incorrect.
explanations.B: Correct. The cloud's pay-as-you-go pricing shifts spending from upfront capital expenditure (CapEx) toward ongoing operational expenditure (OpEx).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The cloud supports structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data; there is no forced shift to only structured data.
explanations.D: Incorrect. In the cloud the provider manages the physical hardware, so the customer's hardware maintenance decreases rather than increases.

question: When an organization adopts cloud technology, how does their total cost of ownership (TCO) shift?

options.A: Away from cost management toward capital expenditure
options.B: Away from operational expenditure toward cost management
options.C: Away from capital expenditure toward operational expenditure
options.D: Away from operational expenditure toward capital expenditure

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud adoption moves away from capital expenditure, not toward it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cloud increases reliance on operational expenditure rather than moving away from it.
explanations.C: Correct. Adopting the cloud shifts spending away from large upfront capital expenditure (buying hardware) toward operational expenditure (paying for what you use), changing how TCO is structured.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The shift is from capital expenditure toward operational expenditure, which is the reverse of this option.

question: Which policy helps Google Cloud keep customer data private?

options.A: Google tests the service availability of customer applications.
options.B: Google does not use customer data for advertising purposes.
options.C: Google migrates customer data to an offline server when a threat is detected.
options.D: Google does not allow customers to change encryption keys.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Testing the availability of customer applications relates to reliability, not data privacy.
explanations.B: Correct. Google Cloud's commitment that it does not use customer data for advertising is a core privacy policy that helps keep customer data private.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Google does not automatically migrate customer data to an offline server when a threat is detected; this is not a stated privacy policy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Google Cloud actually lets customers manage their own encryption keys (for example, with Cloud KMS or CMEK), so this statement is false.
